I have an opinion on the subject of Reddit talk in general (even on Reddit-related subs).

I really hope that the Reddit-mania we're going through right now calms down some, because I think it's going to really hurt the site in the longrun if we don't start focusing on becoming our own thing.

Right now Voat is just a Reddit complaint box and gossip column and because of that it's hard to sell the site to people who don't hate Reddit. I talked a friend into visiting Voat and later when I asked her about it she wrote back that she looked it over, but that just about every sub was dead and the only active posts she noticed were about Reddit. She said that she didn't get 'the point' of Voat since it's 'the same as Reddit, but worse'. (Her words).

It's a problem when new people visit the site and then come to the conclusion that it's a crappier version of Reddit that is only for shit-talking Reddit.

I think that /v/meanwhileonreddit might be the most active sub we have and this isn't great. Just visited their frontpage and nearly everything there has upvotes over 30, many things are way up around 100.

Went to /v/videos and nearly everything is in the single digits or low double digits. One submission towards the bottom of the page is at 54.

/v/news is slightly better with many things over 50, but only two submissions on the front page got over 100 upvotes.

/v/funny is much the same as /v/videos.

I know that 99% of us came from Reddit and it's natural to want to gossip and complain, but we need to do things other than that as well. People other than the mods need to be posting content in non-Reddit bashing subs. I see tons of subs here with great potential and the only person who has ever posted in them is the mod and all he gets is 1 or 2 upvotes.

If you actually want Voat to succeed you need to help out and start posting in subs about things that interest you other than bashing Reddit! The current culture of this site just drives new people back to Reddit.

I've noticed that quite a bit. When we are done bashing Reddit constantly this web site will actually become a decent community.

Unfortunately since every new user is most likely someone who just had a blow out with Reedit, this is unlikely to change for awhile.

I don't care for reddit screenshots, but they should be allowed, even if they are being posted in non-reddit subverses. If the content does not break the rules of the subverse, and is relevant to that subverse, then it should be allowed.

We will most likely see an increase in reddit screenshots, but in time they will die down.

I would rather see content like reddit screenshots fade away because the community shows disgust or a lack of interest, rather than implement content restrictions that go beyond the rules set forth for the individual subverses.
